headline: GOLDSEEK: A TRULY STELLAR DAY — MINING STOCKS 20%+ IN 5 DAYS, SILVER SMASHES $43 RESISTANCE; WHAT COMES NEXT
snippet: GoldSeek published an August 8, 2026 recap identifying Friday August 7 as one of the most decisive single-session confirmations of a new precious metals uptrend in years — a day where gold hit an intraday high of $4,411 (its highest in two months), silver surged 4.16% to $64.10 breaking above key resistance, GDX and GDXJ delivered their fifth consecutive session of gains to complete a five-day move of more than 20% and 22% respectively, and the SIL silver miners ETF blew through the $38–$43 resistance zone that had capped the sector for four months. The analysis identifies several technical and fundamental signals converging simultaneously: the NFP miss that catalysed the Friday surge has reset Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations to zero for 2026, removing the primary macro headwind that had suppressed gold below $4,250 through July; the COT data shows large speculative positions rebuilding on the long side from conviction rather than short-covering; and the GoldSeek piece frames the current setup within the larger cycle context — gold has now gained approximately 150% from its 2022 low, and mining stocks, which had not fully repriced to reflect the underlying metal's gains, have now broken out in a manner that implies they are beginning to close that valuation gap in earnest. For retail investors holding junior mining names through the multi-month correction from gold's $5,598 January high to $3,800, the GoldSeek analysis offers both vindication and a forward-looking setup: the interruption is over, the cyclical advance is resuming, and the coming weeks of Q2 2026 gold earnings reports will provide the fundamental confirmation that the market's technical move has already priced in.

headline: GOLD EYES $4,400+ AS BULL MARKET ACCELERATES — CPI AUG 12, FNV EARNINGS AUG 11 ARE THE PIVOTAL CATALYSTS AHEAD
snippet: Gold enters the week of August 10, 2026 at $4,341 — up approximately 8% in its strongest single week of the year — with three sequential macro data releases that will determine whether the current breakout sustains, reverses, or accelerates: the July Consumer Price Index on Wednesday August 12 (consensus: 2.8%), the July Producer Price Index on Thursday August 13, and the University of Michigan preliminary August inflation expectations on Friday August 14. The StockCharts technical analysis published August 8–9 identifies gold as having broken out above the multi-week resistance zone centred around $4,250, with the intraday high of $4,411 printed on August 7 establishing a new short-term ceiling — and the critical question being whether CPI data will justify gold trading above that level on a sustained basis. The bullish scenario: CPI at or below 2.8% reinforces the zero-rate-hike narrative established by July's -23,000 NFP print, giving gold a macro runway toward $4,500 and ultimately the January 2026 all-time high near $5,598. The risk scenario: a CPI surprise above 3.0% would revive rate-hike speculation and likely trigger a sharp retest of the $4,250 breakout level. Before CPI lands on Wednesday, Franco-Nevada Corp. (TSX/NYSE: FNV) releases Q2 2026 results after Monday's market close — the first royalty company to report for a full quarter at $4,000+ gold, making FNV earnings a real-time stress test of how royalty income scales with the current gold price environment. For junior mining investors watching the sector macro context this week, the sequencing of events — FNV earnings Monday, CPI Wednesday, PPI Thursday — makes this one of the most information-dense five-day windows the gold sector will see in 2026.

headline: DRC BANS COPPER AND COBALT CONCENTRATE EXPORTS — LME COPPER SURGES TO $14,369/T AS SUPPLY CHAIN CONTROL TIGHTENS
snippet: The Democratic Republic of Congo issued a government order effective June 29, 2026 banning exports of copper and cobalt concentrates — announced publicly on August 6, 2026 — in the fourth iteration of this resource-nationalism policy since 2013, this time with the explicit aim of compelling mining companies to process more material inside the country before export. LME copper surged 1.8% on the news, reaching $14,369.50 per tonne — the highest level since January 2026's all-time high — with the combination of the DRC ban, the concurrent Codelco El Teniente Andes Norte production halt, and COMEX copper's confirmed tariff-driven premium over LME creating a trifecta of supply-side pressure on the world's most critical industrial metal. The immediate market impact is limited in volume terms: concentrate exports represented only about 2.6% of the copper in the DRC's reported export streams, meaning this is not a near-term embargo on the country's copper output. Ivanhoe Mines, operator of the world-class Kamoa-Kakula copper mine in the DRC, issued a clarification stating the ban does not materially affect its operations (Kamoa-Kakula already produces finished copper cathode rather than concentrate). However, the policy signal matters beyond its immediate volume impact: each successive iteration of the DRC's concentrate export restriction has been more durable than the last, and for mining companies that had structured their DRC processing around concentrate export assumptions, the order requires capital investment in in-country refining capacity. For junior copper developers in North America and other tariff-exempt jurisdictions, the DRC policy trajectory is a structural argument for the sovereign premium now attached to copper produced outside China-aligned supply chains — a premium that is increasingly reflected in the spread between COMEX and LME copper prices.

headline: CODELCO EL TENIENTE ANDES NORTE HALTED UP TO 2 YEARS ON SEISMIC RISK — WORLD'S LARGEST UNDERGROUND COPPER MINE LIMPING
snippet: Codelco has suspended development of the Andes Norte section at its flagship El Teniente mine — the world's largest underground copper mine — after geological studies identified greater seismic risk than previously understood at the depths required for the expansion, with a union leader stating the halt could last as long as two years. The decision follows six months of analysis triggered by a rockburst on July 31, 2025 that killed six workers and was equivalent to a magnitude-4.2 earthquake, and which remains under criminal, regulatory, and technical investigation. Andes Norte is adjacent to the Andesita and Teniente 7 mining areas, meaning the suspension affects planned production capacity at one of Chile's most critical copper-producing assets. The operational context is severe: El Teniente's copper production was already approximately 27% lower year-over-year in the first five months of 2026, and Codelco's new chairman has acknowledged that the company's goal of returning to 1.7 million tonnes of annual copper production by 2030 is no longer achievable on the originally planned timeline. For the global copper market, the Codelco development comes simultaneously with the DRC concentrate export ban and COMEX copper trading near all-time highs on tariff-driven pre-loading — three distinct supply-chain stress signals at once, all pointing in the same direction. Chile produces approximately 25% of global copper supply, and El Teniente alone represents roughly 380,000 tonnes per year of capacity. A two-year delay in the Andes Norte expansion is not a closure — but it removes expected growth tonnes from an already supply-constrained market in the exact window (2026–2027) when copper demand from AI data centres, EV manufacturing, and grid electrification is expected to accelerate most sharply.

headline: FOUNDERS METALS: 28m AT 14.27 g/t AU FROM 433m DEPTH — HIGH-GRADE DEEP HIT EXTENDS ANTINO GOLD SYSTEM IN SURINAME (FDR.V)
snippet: Founders Metals Inc. (TSXV: FDR, OTCQB: FDMIF) reported August 6, 2026 results from drill hole FR249 at the Upper Antino target of its Antino Gold Project in southeastern Suriname — a 50-metre down-dip extension of previously reported hole FR175 (10.0m of 5.90 g/t gold) that returned 28.0 metres at 14.27 g/t gold from 433.0 metres depth. The grade improvement from FR175 to FR249 is structurally significant: the new hole, drilled 50 metres deeper into the system and 50 metres in the down-dip direction, not only maintained grade but substantially improved it — 14.27 g/t versus 5.90 g/t — indicating that the mineralisation is becoming higher-grade with depth rather than deteriorating, a characteristic associated with preserved, unoxidised gold deposits that benefit from increasing structural control at depth. According to President & CEO Colin Padget, the Upper Antino system was previously traced to approximately 500 metres vertical in earlier deep drilling, and FR249 now confirms that the deeper horizons carry substantially higher grades than the near-surface portions of the same structure. The geological interpretation centres on the gabbro body intersected at depth: the competent, brittle unit fractures preferentially where the mineralising shear zones cut through it, creating higher permeability conduits for gold-bearing hydrothermal fluids while its iron-rich composition promotes gold deposition. For junior investors monitoring the Antino project's evolution from explorer to advanced-stage developer, a 28-metre interval at over 14 g/t gold from 433 metres depth — in a jurisdiction with a strong mining framework, good infrastructure, and a growing resource database — is the type of deep high-grade extension that opens underground mining scenarios with materially different economics than the near-surface portions of the deposit.

headline: PERPETUA RESOURCES STIBNITE: GOLD + ANTIMONY + TUNGSTEN ZONES CONFIRMED ALONGSIDE $1.3B MINE CONSTRUCTION (PPTA)
snippet: Perpetua Resources Corp. (NASDAQ: PPTA) reported August 6, 2026 the results of the first exploratory drilling at its Stibnite Gold-Antimony project in central Idaho in nearly a decade, confirming multiple new high-grade intercepts across gold, antimony, and — in a significant expansion of the critical minerals story — tungsten. Key intercepts from the Yellow Pine zone include 21.3 metres grading 3.2 g/t gold and 0.9% tungsten and 6.4 metres at 16.2 g/t gold and 1.7% antimony. The Hangar Flats zone contributed 22.9 metres at 3.2% antimony and 1.2% tungsten, establishing tungsten as a credible third critical mineral at a project that was already one of the most strategically important domestic mining developments in the United States — the only significant domestic antimony-gold project in the country, with a $2.9 billion Department of Energy loan secured in May 2026 and $1.3 billion of mine construction already underway. The tungsten discovery is particularly strategically significant: tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal and is considered irreplaceable for defence applications (armour-piercing munitions, missile guidance systems) and advanced manufacturing, and US domestic tungsten supply is essentially non-existent — the country imports nearly 100% of its tungsten requirements, primarily from China. The combination of gold, antimony, and now tungsten at a single vertically integrated, federally-financed Idaho project represents a rare convergence of US critical mineral policy priorities, and the new drill results suggest the permitted resource at Stibnite is materially larger than currently modelled. Perpetua is seeking US grant funding to conduct a full resource evaluation of the newly identified zones.

headline: AZTEC MINERALS: 88.4m AT 1.69 g/t AUEQ IN FIRST NORTH EXTENSION STEP-OUT — TOMBSTONE ARIZONA MAIDEN RESOURCE APPROACHING (AZT.V)
snippet: Aztec Minerals Corp. (TSXV: AZT, OTCQB: AZZTF) announced August 5, 2026 assay results from nine reverse-circulation drill holes at its 100%-owned Tombstone Project in southeastern Arizona — the first step-out drilling into the recently acquired North Extension Zone — with highlight hole TR26-39 returning 88.4 metres grading 1.42 g/t gold and 14.58 g/t silver (1.69 g/t gold equivalent) including a 6.1-metre high-grade core at 12.23 g/t gold and 56.28 g/t silver. A second hole, TR26-38, intersected 97.5 metres at 1.06 g/t gold from surface — a bulk-tonnage near-surface intercept that, combined with the high-grade North Extension step-out, is expanding the footprint of what was already identified as a large near-surface oxide gold-silver system suitable for heap-leach processing. Aztec has now completed 90 reverse-circulation holes in its 2025–2026 drill programme, with assay results still pending for 11 additional step-out holes testing the northern and depth extensions of the mineralised system. The company is targeting a maiden mineral resource estimate based on the completed drill database — a milestone that would transition Tombstone from a pre-resource exploration project to a resource-stage asset with defined tonnes and grade, triggering re-rating consideration from investors who only engage with companies that have established resources. The project is located in Arizona, a Tier 1 US mining jurisdiction, with mineralisation classified as near-surface oxide gold-silver — the ideal metallurgical profile for low-capital heap-leach construction. At $4,300+ gold and $64 silver, the economics of a heap-leach scenario on 88–97 metre-wide near-surface oxide intercepts across multiple drill holes are compelling, and the pending step-out holes could further expand the resource footprint before the estimate is completed.

headline: CHINA'S ZIJIN DROPS $5.5B ALLIED GOLD BID — TAKES 9.2% STAKE AT $295M INSTEAD; AFRICA RISK AND BEIJING RULES CITED
snippet: China's Zijin Mining Group abandoned its proposed C$5.5 billion (US$3.9 billion) takeover of Allied Gold Corp. (TSX: AGLD) on July 29, 2026 — what would have been Zijin's largest-ever proposed acquisition — instead taking a 9.2% strategic stake in Allied for US$295 million by subscribing to 12.8 million Allied common shares at C$32.55 per share (the 30-day VWAP). The collapse of the full takeover is attributable to a combination of factors: Chinese regulatory headwinds from Beijing's growing concern over outbound capital flows, tightened rules on overseas investments in politically sensitive jurisdictions, and mounting geopolitical risk associated with Allied's flagship asset base in the Sahel region of West Africa — particularly the Mali operations, where Fekola mine's Menankoto exploitation permit has been pending regulatory approval from the Malian military government. The deal's failure is a landmark data point for the Canadian junior mining sector: Zijin was willing to commit US$295 million but not US$3.9 billion to the same African gold assets, effectively quantifying the discount that Chinese institutional capital is now applying to African mining exposure where sovereign risk is elevated. Allied Gold will direct the US$295 million in net proceeds toward advancing the Kurmuk gold mine start-up in Ethiopia, phased expansion at Sadiola in Mali, production growth at the CDI complex, and ongoing exploration — maintaining its growth trajectory without the completion risk of a full change-of-control transaction. The episode illustrates the increasingly complex M&A calculus in gold mining: at $4,300+ gold, seller valuations are at cycle highs, but Chinese buyer constraint combined with western M&A caution about Africa means the gap between what sellers want and what buyers will commit continues to produce partial transactions rather than full acquisitions.

headline: BOFA: GOLD MINERS AT 19% NAV DISCOUNT, FCF 10X 2020 LEVELS — 'COMPELLING VALUE' DESPITE PRICE TARGET CUT TO $4,360
snippet: Bank of America's global commodities research team published a note arguing that gold mining stocks represent compelling value even after the bank trimmed its 2026 gold price forecast by 14% to $4,360 per ounce — essentially the current spot price level — because the valuation case for miners is built on operational metrics rather than price upside alone. The bank's analysis identifies gold mining stocks as trading at a 19% discount to net asset value, with free cash flow generation approximately 10 times higher than 2020 levels at current gold prices, and long-term debt as a percentage of equity cut in half over the past three years — a balance sheet transformation that means gold producers are now harvesting the benefits of investment cycles that were funded at much lower gold prices. BofA's top sector picks include Agnico Eagle for gold exposure, Freeport-McMoRan for copper demand growth, and Cameco for uranium's role in the global nuclear energy buildout. The broader message from BofA is one that resonates with the retail investor thesis for junior miners: if the world's largest investment banks are now identifying major gold producers as structurally undervalued at $4,360 gold — mining at 19% discounts to their asset values — the pricing anomaly is even more pronounced for junior developers and near-production explorers, which historically trade at steeper discounts to NAV than majors and then rerate sharply when gold sector sentiment improves. With GDX and GDXJ delivering 20%+ five-day moves as the sector breakout accelerates, the BofA analysis provides institutional-grade fundamental support for what the technical picture is already signalling: the repricing of gold mining equities relative to the underlying metal has barely started.

headline: FRANCO-NEVADA Q2 2026 RESULTS DUE MONDAY AUG 11 — FIRST FULL QUARTER AT $4,000+ GOLD EXPECTED TO SET ROYALTY RECORDS (FNV)
snippet: Franco-Nevada Corporation (TSX/NYSE: FNV), the world's largest gold-focused royalty and streaming company, will release second-quarter 2026 financial results after market close on Monday August 11, 2026, with a conference call scheduled for Tuesday August 12 at 8:00 a.m. ET — the same morning as July's Consumer Price Index release. As a royalty company, Franco-Nevada receives a fixed percentage of revenue from the mines on its royalty portfolio without bearing operating costs, capital expenditures, or exploration risk — meaning its royalty income scales directly with the gold price and is largely insulated from cost inflation that compresses producer margins. Q2 2026 (April 1 through June 30) was the first full quarter in which gold prices were sustained above $4,000 per ounce throughout the entire period, translating directly into Franco-Nevada's largest absolute royalty income quarter on record. The conference call coinciding with CPI creates an unusual information double-event on August 12 that will either reinforce or complicate the current gold bull case: strong FNV Q2 results demonstrating the profitability of royalty structures at $4,000+ gold, followed immediately by the July CPI print that determines whether gold can sustain and extend above $4,300. FNV currently has royalty interests on more than 400 mineral properties globally, including cornerstone positions on Cobre Panama, Antapaccay, and the Hemlo stream. Analysts rate FNV as Outperform driven by high margins, near-zero leverage, and ample liquidity to deploy on new royalty acquisitions — a combination that, at $4,300 gold, turns a defensive royalty structure into a high-growth compounding machine.

headline: FORMER SIBANYE CEO FRONEMAN PLANS SEAWATER URANIUM MINING COMPANY — AMBITIOUS TECH BET ON NUCLEAR'S AI FUTURE
snippet: Neal Froneman, who led Sibanye-Stillwater as President and CEO for 13 years before stepping down at age 65 in late 2025, announced August 7, 2026 plans to establish a new mining company focused on extracting uranium from seawater — one of the most ambitious and technically challenging concepts in the uranium supply space. The ocean contains an estimated 4.5 billion tonnes of dissolved uranium at approximately 3.3 parts per billion, representing a theoretical reserve more than 1,000 times greater than all known terrestrial uranium deposits combined. The challenge is extraction: current seawater uranium harvesting technology using polymer adsorbent systems can recover uranium at a cost estimated at US$300–600 per pound — compared to the current spot price of approximately US$86.50 per pound — making the economics viable only with a dramatic cost reduction. Froneman's argument is that a combination of scale, materials science advances (particularly in high-capacity uranium-selective adsorbents), and the long-term structural demand outlook driven by AI data centre nuclear commitments (Meta and Microsoft have both signed agreements for dedicated nuclear capacity) justifies investing in the technology now, at the bottom of the cost curve, when intellectual property can be accumulated before the market catches on. The initiative draws on Froneman's deep track record of executing technically ambitious mining strategies — Sibanye's platinum and battery metals diversification under his leadership was broadly regarded as one of the most successful mining group transformations of the 2010s. The seawater uranium thesis is early-stage and carries substantial technology risk, but the underlying demand dynamics — nuclear power as the only reliable 24/7 renewable-equivalent baseload energy source for AI infrastructure — are concrete.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD, SILVER AND MINING STOCKS POISED TO EXPLODE HIGHER — TECHNICAL CASE FOR NEXT MAJOR LEG UP (AUG 8)
snippet: A GoldSeek technical analysis published August 8, 2026 argues that gold, silver, and mining stocks have completed the technical setup for the most powerful advance of their current bull market — a view grounded in the simultaneous breakout of multiple previously resistant indicators. The analysis identifies five concurrent technical signals that historically precede major precious metals advances: (1) GDX and GDXJ both breaking above multi-month consolidation resistance on significantly above-average volume; (2) SIL (silver miners ETF) clearing the $43 level that had been a ceiling for four consecutive months; (3) gold closing above $4,300 — a level that had been tested and rejected three times since June — on a weekly basis; (4) the gold-silver ratio compressing from above 70x toward the mid-60s, historically associated with institutional capital rotating from gold to silver in mid-cycle; and (5) commercial hedger positioning in COMEX gold futures at a level of net short exposure consistent with prior market peaks but with speculative net long positioning still below historical cycle highs, indicating that the current move has not yet attracted the excess speculation that historically precedes corrections. Fundamentally, the piece contextualises the technical setup within the earnings season about to begin: gold producers reporting Q2 2026 results at $4,000+ gold versus $2,200 gold in Q2 2024 will show a near-doubling of per-ounce margins in the space of two years, with free cash flow at many miners now sufficient to retire all debt within two to three years at current prices. For silver investors specifically, the analysis identifies the metal's 1980 inflation-adjusted all-time high above $150 per ounce as the structural long-term target, and the recent SIL breakout as the technical trigger that historically precedes silver's most powerful advances relative to gold.
